title: PIGen: Accelerating ReRAM Co-Design via Generative Physics-Informed Modeling
problem: Optimizing ReRAM device parameters across diverse materials and operating conditions is challenging for data-intensive computing applications.
motivation: Efficient ReRAM design requires bridging device physics with system-level performance targets while handling sparse experimental data.
method: PIGen uses a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to model ReRAM switching dynamics with physical constraints, combined with a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) to generate optimized design parameters from performance targets (endurance, latency, energy).
key_novelty: Integrating physics-informed learning with generative design for automated ReRAM parameter optimization across materials.
contributions: PINN-based device modeling with sparse training data
CVAE-based generative system for parameter synthesis
limitations: Relies on PINN accuracy which depends on training data quality; limited discussion of transferability across material families.
primary_theme: Physics-informed generative modeling for memory device design
